The statement balances robust domestic demand and labor-market strength with significant adverse supply shocks. In New Keynesian frameworks (e.g., Galí), pandemic disruptions and energy price shocks shift the Phillips curve outward, creating an inflation–output tradeoff. Empirical work on energy price shocks shows they raise inflation while dampening growth, consistent with the FOMC’s concern that the invasion and related events “are likely to weigh on economic activity.” The policy response—raising the policy rate and beginning balance-sheet reduction—aligns with inflation-forecast targeting principles (Svensson and Woodford) and Taylor-style prescriptions, which can help re-anchor expectations. However, tighter financial conditions typically depress business fixed investment through credit-sensitive channels (Bernanke–Gertler), implying downside risks to near-term activity despite current job gains. Net tone: slightly negative, with credible policy partly mitigating the risks.
